_note: M-MODES WeaponCatalog (docs/spec/modes.md §3). EVERY weapon is now based on ITS OWN captured Callsign $WEAP frame (`capture.frame`, traced to `capture.src` in protocol/captures/raw/; regenerate the decode with `python -m brx_mcp.weapmap protocol/captures/raw/*.btsnoop`; named table in docs/reference/weapons.md). That inherits every native behaviour we cannot synthesise: 3-round burst (t23), bolt/single-shot, charge, overheat (t24/t35), per-weapon reload chains, damage type (t3), reload type (t19), muzzle flash (t25/t26). `reload_type` (F123, 2026-09-11) is an EXPLICIT per-weapon attribute and is deliberately NOT read off `capture.frame` t19: t19 is unconfirmed as reloadType (the Plasma Sniper shell-reloads at t19=0 — protocol/callsign-extract/protocol-classes.md), so the only value set here is the one the wire actually proved. 'chain' = the reload is a HELD per-shell chain, `reload_ms` is the PER-SHELL interval, and a momentary button cannot drive it (the Shotgun: after $BUT,2,1 the $ALCD mag walks 1→6 at 417/423/390/420/420 ms, one reserve decrement per shell). Absent = a normal magazine reload. `wire` lists ONLY the tokens we deliberately overwrite for balance; mag/reserve/reload_ms are written too (t16/t39, t17/t40, t18) keeping the captured invariants t39==t16 and t17==2*t40. Everything else is emitted byte-for-byte as Battle Company sent it. stats: dmg/rof/rng are 0-100 UI bars derived from the real numbers. dmg = share of a 115 pool one hit removes, rof = cycle relative to the fastest weapon, rng = the wire's t41 gunRange (identical on all 18 guns: range is NOT differentiated on the wire today; see weapon-design.md §4.2). 'verified' now means SHIPPED EXACTLY AS CAPTURED (no balance edit); 'captured' is true for all 19. 'melee' is hidden (slot 4). tags: policy vocabulary (docs/spec/loadout.md §1.1). 'heavy' = role power (rocket/rail/laser cannon/energy launcher/ion sniper), 'sniper' = the four long guns incl. AMR, plus the role name; presets exclude by tag so a new weapon only needs the right tags. `class` (2026-09-17, arsenal review): 'ballistic' | 'energy' | 'melee', on every row; ballistic weapons reload, energy weapons overheat or charge. `hidden` (2026-09-17 arsenal cut): force_rifle, bolt_rifle, stinger, plasma_sniper, laser_cannon, ion_sniper, energy_launcher and glock are hidden from the picker alongside melee, cutting overlap in a 22-weapon catalogue; the row and its capture frame stay (custom games, and the pistols' based_on copy of bolt_rifle's frame, still use them). `pickup_only` (2026-09-17): rocket_launcher, rail_gun, laser_cannon, ion_sniper and energy_launcher (the 'heavy' tag) are never in a player's starting loadout pool, whatever the preset; they stay in the catalogue for a future pickup/station mechanism (docs/spec/loadout.md). `rounds_per_charge` (2026-09-17, F226/S43 bench): on the Charge Rifle only, one full charge costs this many rounds of the `mag`/`reserve` cell (10, bench-measured); every place that turns `mag`/`reserve` into a hits-or-kills count for this weapon must divide by it first (`mag // rounds_per_charge` full charges), never read the raw round count as a hit count. Absent = 1 (every other weapon fires one round per hit). caution: optional human copy for a weapon with a known LIVE problem. The UIs show it on the tile and hero. based_on (2026-09-04, sidearms): a weapon with NO capture of its own names the captured weapon whose frame it is built on and why; its capture block is a COPY of that frame (same src), `captured: false`, and every deviation is a wire/override token. 'sidearm' = the three pistols (usp/glock/deagle, role sidearm, cls 10): slot-2 backups by design, deliberately dominated by primaries (test_ttk_band exempts them from BEING dominated, never from dominating). Fire sounds P16/Q04/X14 (glock/usp/deagle, ear-confirmed 2026-09-11) are ids no other weapon uses, so a custom .LTP over the data port (community-notes.md) replaces only that pistol.

weapons.name: Assault Rifle
weapons.desc: The anchor, and the real stock M4 cadence. 13 hits at 100ms with 32 up and 192 in reserve: 17 kills without resupply and a 1.20s kill. 2026-09-17 arsenal review: cycle is back to Battle Company's native 100ms (it was throttled to 140ms so a deep reserve could not also out-cycle the field); the dominance test now grades on one-magazine kill chance rather than total kills, so the reserve alone no longer has to carry the whole weight of keeping the AR in check.

weapons.name: Burst Rifle
weapons.desc: A real three-round burst: one pull, three rounds, and the gun enforces the gap. 11 hits from a 36-round mag with 216 behind it; the most total ammo of the burst pair, and the tighter of the two. 2026-09-17 arsenal review: damage raised 9 to 11 so the burst pair separates further from the SMG-class assault weapons on hits-to-kill, not only on cadence.

weapons.name: Force Rifle
weapons.desc: The burst rifle's heavier twin: same three-round pull, more per round. 12 hits instead of 13 and a faster kill, paid for with two-thirds the reserve and a slower five-part reload.

t33.why: captured D21 plays a 'disable' chirp alongside the reload, reproduced on the bench 2026-08-26; D02 is the clean cocking beat the AR/burst/bolt chains already end on

weapons.name: Bolt Rifle
weapons.desc: Single shot, deliberate cadence. 13 a hit every 225ms with 18 up and 180 back. That is 22 kills from a full kit, for operators who would rather aim than hold.

weapons.name: SMG
weapons.desc: A hose that runs hot. 8 a hit every 95ms from a 72-round mag: four kills before you reload, 24 across the kit, and an overheat budget that punishes holding the trigger down forever.

weapons.name: Shotgun
weapons.desc: Shell by shell, and the fastest recovery on the board. 45 a hit at 800ms, three hits to drop, six in the tube and a 400ms shell reload. Sustained pressure from the shallowest ammo pool outside the power tier.

weapons.name: Stinger
weapons.desc: Fast, light, relentless. 15 a hit every 250ms with 18 up and 144 in reserve: eight hits to drop, twenty kills to spend, and nothing held back for range.

weapons.name: Sniper Rifle
weapons.desc: Two hits, one lane, a bolt between them. 60 a hit on a 1.5s cycle with four in the mag and 24 behind it. The fewest hits to a kill outside the power tier, and no margin for a miss.

t33.why: captured D21 plays a 'disable' chirp alongside the reload, reproduced on the bench 2026-08-26; D02 is the clean cocking beat the AR/burst/bolt chains already end on

weapons.name: Plasma Sniper
weapons.desc: A marksman rifle that fires like a carbine and pays for it in heat. 25 a hit every 400ms, five to drop, ten up and 80 back. Lean on it and it overheats.

weapons.name: AMR
weapons.desc: Anti-materiel weight at a rifle's cadence. 24 a hit every 400ms, five hits to a kill, 14 up and only 56 behind. The hardest-hitting automatic, and the shallowest.
weapons.range_target_m: full reach indoor / 60m+ outdoor (Q15, tagged sniper)

t33.why: captured D21 plays a 'disable' chirp alongside the reload, reproduced on the bench 2026-08-26; D02 is the clean cocking beat the AR/burst/bolt chains already end on

weapons.name: Suppressor
weapons.desc: Quiet, not silent, and no muzzle flash. It is the only weapon here that hides where you are. 8 a hit every 140ms with 75 up and 384 in reserve: 30 kills, the deepest magazine AND the deepest sustained pool, the slowest kill. 2026-09-17: mag 48→75 -- the family-scoped dominance test (§2.3) paired it against the SMG (same fire mode, same weapon_class), which beat it on every other axis; the deeper magazine gives the Suppressor an outright lead on kills-per-clip (5 vs the SMG's 4), which is the smallest change that stops the SMG strictly dominating it.
weapons.range_target_m: 15 indoor / 30 outdoor (Q15, as the LMG-role deep-mag automatic)

weapons.caution: Overheats after about 30 rounds of full auto, and it does not cool on its own: HOLD the reload lever to vent the heat, then keep holding to recharge the cell.
weapons.name: Energy Rifle
weapons.desc: A 300-cell battery that barely stops. 9 a hit every 150ms, 23 kills on one magazine and 69 across the kit. The largest ammo pool in the game, on the smallest per-hit number. 2026-09-17 bench (F229): now genuinely overheats — full auto locks it out around heat 99 after about 30 shots, and unlike the Charge Rifle it does not cool on its own; only the reload lever (a hold, not a tap) vents it.
weapons.range_target_m: 15 indoor / 30 outdoor (Q15, as the LMG-role deep-mag automatic)

t38.why: F229 bench, 2026-09-17: t38 = 150 alone switches the Energy Rifle's overheat on (captured at t38 blank, so it shipped inert). Heat climbs about +3 net per shot, locks at about 99 (roughly 30 shots), and does not fall on its own while locked -- the reload lever is hold-to-recharge, and the SAME hold that refills the cell vents the heat; there is no separate cooldown. A lockout clears only by working the lever, about three taps or one held pull

t35.why: F229 bench, 2026-09-17, ear-confirmed by Tony on a real overheat ("yeah nice"): D11 (the SMG's captured overheat sound) is right. The captured D122 "sounds like it reloaded", not overheated

weapons.name: Charge Rifle
weapons.desc: Pre-charge it behind cover, then the kill is one release and two taps: an 85-damage charge (held indefinitely, 3.5s by feel to build although the wire's t14 reads 1250ms) plus two 20-damage taps drops a 115 pool in about 1s from release -- 3 trigger actions, 12 of the 40 rounds up, 84 of the roughly-103 heat budget (S43). The charge time is setup, not combat time: that is the weapon's identity. Forty up, eighty back -- three combo kills a magazine, ten across the kit.
weapons.range_target_m: 18-20 indoor / 40-45 outdoor (Q15, an ambush weapon needs the target closed, not far)

weapons.name: Glock-18
weapons.desc: The middle ground. 13 a hit at a measured cadence, 9 hits to drop, 16 in the mag with 64 behind it: 8 kills across the kit. Not the fastest trigger and not the biggest punch, but the safest bet not to be caught reloading.

based_on.why: no Callsign sidearm was ever captured; the Bolt Rifle frame is the one captured semi-automatic (t20=7, one shot per pull, no bolt pair, magazine reload) so it inherits the right trigger behaviour and $SIR row. Every deviation is a named wire/override token below.

t27.why: Glock-18 fire sound: ear 2026-09-11, P16 ("Deagle sound") preferred for the Glock over the earlier P09 ("a pronounced shot, could be the Deagle"); P09 is now unused. P16 is used by no other weapon, so a custom .LTP swapped in over the data port replaces only this pistol's shot

weapons.name: USP-S
weapons.desc: The quiet one. Suppressed and flashless: 9 a hit, as fast as you can pull the trigger, 13 hits to drop, 19 in the mag with 120 behind it: 10 kills across the kit. Low damage, but nobody hears where it came from. 2026-09-17: mag 20→19 -- Tony's ask was 20→14, but 14 leaves the Deagle strictly dominating the USP (its sustained DPS and one-magazine kill chance both fall too far once the mag is that shallow); 19 is the smallest cut off 20 that actually leaves neither pistol beating the other on every axis (a thin margin: sustained DPS differs by about 0.1 dmg/s, kill chance by 2 points).

weapons.name: Desert Eagle
weapons.desc: The hand cannon. 26 a hit, five hits to drop — the most damage of any sidearm, if you land them. Seven in the mag, 48 behind it: 11 kills across the kit. A slow cycle that punishes every miss.

based_on.why: no Callsign sidearm was ever captured; the Bolt Rifle frame is the one captured semi-automatic (t20=7, one shot per pull, no bolt pair, magazine reload) so it inherits the right trigger behaviour and $SIR row. Every deviation is a named wire/override token below.

weapons.name: Rocket Launcher
weapons.desc: Point, pull, erase. 115 a hit (a full-health operator in one) on the fastest power-tier cycle, with the slowest reload behind it. Four rounds, four kills, no second chances.
weapons.range_target_m: 18-20 indoor / 40-45 outdoor (Q15, not bench-set: a power weapon, not a marksman one)

weapons.name: Rail Gun
weapons.desc: Charges and fires itself. A 1.2s wind-up that goes whether you are ready or not, 115 on impact, four rounds total. Everyone within earshot hears the spool.
weapons.range_target_m: 18-20 indoor / 40-45 outdoor (Q15, not bench-set: a power weapon, not a marksman one)

weapons.name: Laser Cannon
weapons.desc: Must be held to charge; a tap fires nothing at all. 1.5s of commitment for a guaranteed kill, and the fastest reload in the power tier for the trouble.

weapons.name: Energy Launcher
weapons.desc: No charge, no tell, no warning. 115 a hit with the fastest reload on the board and the slowest cycle in its tier. Four kills, spent quietly.

t27.why: ear 2026-09-11 (W4a audition, six O-family clips solo): O06 ("shooting a rocket") chosen over the earlier placeholder O01; O04 ("shooting a missile") was runner-up, O01/O02/O05 read as the BLAST not the launch, and O03 is a rifle shot. Original placeholder rationale: captured J15 is a music sting (J = music/SFX family, DK legend), inherited from the 'unnamed secondary' frame (bench 2026-08-26); the O family is otherwise unused by the stock arsenal

weapons.caution: Known issue: deals no damage in our shipped config (weapon-design.md). Avoid until fixed.

weapons.name: Ion Sniper
weapons.desc: A one-shot kill in a rifle's body. 115 a hit on a 1.4s cycle with two up and two back. The power tier's only weapon that looks and sounds like a marksman rifle.

weapons.name: Melee
weapons.desc: Last resort: no ammo, no reload, a gyro swing with the butt of the gun. 90 on contact. Hidden from the picker, always bound to slot 4.
